'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (2026)|Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon]]
****[[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli defence minister]] [[Israel Katz]] says [[Israel Defense Forces|his forces]] will not withdraw from [[Israeli-occupied territories|occupied]] [[southern Lebanon]] even if "the [[United States]] demands it", adding that "200,000 residents will not return" to their homes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/6/24/iran-war-live-trump-tehran-at-odds-over-nuclear-inspections-hormuz (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] announces that it has killed [[Hamas]] militant Akram Muhammad Mahmoud Abu Machi, who took part in the [[October 7 attacks]] on [[Israel]], during an [[airstrike]] in southern [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-says-it-killed-hamas-terrorist-who-took-part-in-oct-7-planned-future-attacks/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/429143 (''Israel National News'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] launch long-range [[drone warfare|drone strikes]] inside [[Russia]], striking the [[Orenburg gas field|Orenburg Gas Processing Plant]], which also houses the only [[helium]] plant in Russia, and also striking two [[Russian Satellite Communications Company]] facilities, including one in [[Moscow Oblast]] and another in [[Vladimir Oblast]]. Russia says [[Russian Armed Forces|its forces]] have shot down 323 Ukrainian drones overnight. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-crimea-attacks-6076b6666c3312bbf9b4b8d875a52513 (AP)]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***Ukrainian [[missile]]s strike two [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]] airfields and several [[Anti-aircraft warfare|air defence systems]] in [[Crimea]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-crimea-attacks-6076b6666c3312bbf9b4b8d875a52513 (AP)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[War crimes during the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|War crimes during the Sudanese civil war]]
***The [[Sudan Doctors Network]] reports that more than 215 civilians have died at the [[Rapid Support Forces|RSF]]-run Daqris Prison in [[Sudan]]'s [[South Darfur]] [[States of Sudan|state]] from the spread of [[disease|diseases]] and [[epidemic|epidemics]], as well as [[torture]] and mistreatment of detainees. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/215-civilians-die-in-rsf-run-prison-in-south-darfur-sudanese-medics/3976982 (AA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 United States wildfires]]
**[[2026 Colorado wildfires]]
***A [[wildfire]] burns over 350 acres and destroys a home in [[Garfield County, Colorado|Garfield County]], [[Colorado]], [[United States|U.S.]], prompting evacuations. **[[2026 Utah wildfires]]
***The [[Cottonwood Fire (Utah, 2026)|Cottonwood Fire]] burns over 59,000 acres near the Eagle Point Resort in [[Beaver, Utah|Beaver]], [[Utah]], U.S., with [[Governor of Utah|governor]] [[Spencer Cox]] saying it is the "most destructive fire in the [[History of Utah|state’s history]]". [https://www.sltrib.com/news/2026/06/24/cottonwood-fire-burns-eagle-point/ (''The Salt Lake Tribune'')]

Severe damage and collapsed buildings are recorded in [[Caracas]], with casualties being unknown. [https://apnews.com/article/venezuela-earthquake-caracas-7179acaee70a9c543f953852f15d4814 (AP)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/24/world/americas/earthquake-venezuela.html (''The New York Times'')].

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**[[France]] confirms its first [[Ebola]] case, and the first case identified outside [[Africa]] in this outbreak, after a humanitarian worker returns from the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [[French National Public Health Agency|French health authorities]] isolate the patient and begin [[contact tracing]]. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/health-science/2026/6/24/france-detects-first-ebola-case-outside-africa-in-current-outbreak-1815 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/06/24/world/france-ebola-patient (CNN)]
*[[Sri Lanka]] begins enforcing a nationwide ban on the sale and provision of foods and drinks high in sugar, salt, and fat in [[Education in Sri Lanka|schools]] as part of measures to address rising [[childhood obesity]] and related [[Health in Sri Lanka|health]] conditions. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/south-asia/sri-lanka-bans-junk-food-in-schools-due-to-health-concerns (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*The [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] says that it will require recruits to take the [[influenza vaccine]] amidst an [[influenza]] outbreak at the [[Lackland Air Force Base]] in [[Bexar County, Texas|Bexar County]], [[Texas]], U.S. The move comes after [[United States Secretary of Defense|U.S. defense secretary]] [[Pete Hegseth]] lifted the military [[vaccine]] mandate. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/military-flu-vaccine-recruits-hegseth-lackland-outbreak/ (CBS News)] [https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/us-military-requires-flu-vaccine-some-after-outbreak-texas-training-center-2026-06-24/ (Reuters)]

*[[2026 Colombian presidential election]]
**[[Historic Pact]]'s candidate [[Iván Cepeda]] concedes defeat in the [[President of Colombia|presidential]] election won by [[Abelardo de la Espriella]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgrkqky5lzpo (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA World Cup]]
**[[Bosnia and Herzegovina at the FIFA World Cup]], [[Canada at the FIFA World Cup]], [[South Africa at the FIFA World Cup]]
***In [[association football]], [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa]] reaches the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]] of a [[FIFA World Cup]] for the first time after defeating [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] 1–0 in their final group-stage match to finish second in [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group A|Group A]]. Co-hosts [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] and [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] also advance for the first time after finishing [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B|Group B]] in second place and [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third place]], respectively. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260625-south-africa-stun-south-korea-to-make-world-cup-history (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260624-bosnia-in-strong-position-to-reach-last-32-qatar-out-of-world-cup (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49168179/canada-qualify-world-cup-knockouts-miss-chance-top-group-switzerland (ESPN)]
*[[FIFA]] suspends [[Football in Nepal|Nepal]]'s [[All Nepal Football Association|football association]] with immediate effect for violating [[FIFA Disciplinary Code|its statutes]] through third-party interference, barring [[Nepal]] from [[Association football#International competitions|international football]] competitions until the conditions for reinstatement are met. [https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/football/news/fifa-suspends-nepal-over-third-party-interference-4208216 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]
